items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Budd said that he personally would put the proposition to Basie which he did. Bill (Basie) was very understanding about the deal...

ctx.x: One week after the visit of "Wild Bill" and his friend, they came back to Woodlawn Inn and Bill wanted to play my horn again, but he was so drunk that he could hardly stand. I let him blow my horn but he really didn't play anything that night and I had my revenge because I blew him out. His friend came to get him and put him in a back room where he immediately went to sleep.

Then this friend of Bill's came back to talk with us and it was then that he noticed the playing of Edgar Hayes and it hit him like a man being hit on his head with a blackjack. He asked Edgar to play some numbers that we didn't know and after two or three numbers almost everyone at the Inn that night was standing around the bandstand listening to the pianist. We, in the orchestra were all ears as we were every night when Edgar played. This night we were very proud of him because we had never had a crowd of…

A few nights later, this friend of "Wild Bill's" came back to the Inn alone and said that he came especially to talk to Edgar Hayes. When it came time for us to have our nightly meal, this fellow came into the dining room and sat at the table with us and he did the talking.
